originality.rationale: Katriel 2012 previously proves precisely the lower CV-dependent final-size endpoint and general Laplace-order implication; Izyumtseva et al. 2026 supply the pressure ODE and Jensen bound. The stated finite-cap sharp upper endpoint, attained whole-time two-moment identified interval and explicit fourth-order gap are absent from the materially inspected source statements. General moment extremality is prior methodology, and an unindexed specialized application remains possible.
residual_risks: Existing general Markov–Krein principal representations cover the static sharp Laplace inequality; a specialized epidemic formulation may have appeared outside indexed sources.

value.rationale: Katriel 2012 proves fixed mean and CV cannot improve the homogeneous upper attack-size bound without further restrictions. Imposing an epidemiologically interpretable hard susceptibility cap yields a strict, attained upper bound and a complete uncertainty interval simultaneously across all observation times. Matched moment distributions in the exact illustrative case yield removed fraction approximately 0.53145 to 0.77452. A fourth-order onset coefficient quantifies the first moment-invisible epidemic divergence; this is a substantive identifiability and robust forecasting statement, not a routine numerical recalculation.
